limitations: The probe records arguments and return values as process-independent classes: pointers cannot be compared by value because heap addresses differ, so only the class (null/small-exact/pointer) is comparable.

Retail and the candidate are captured one at a time because both hold a single-instance mutex, and the two runs attach at different points of level load, so call indices, call counts and per-call arguments do not correspond. Only the return-value class set is compared.
A captured call proves the native was reached in both images and that both returned the same class of value; it does not prove behavioural parity and does not establish any side effect.
